commands.notes: Watch uses the same single play/pause control shape as the iPhone playback surface; phone/tablet executes the toggle and returns a refreshed compact snapshot.
Watch sends a play intent to the canonical phone/tablet runtime and expects a refreshed compact snapshot response.
Watch sends a pause intent to the canonical phone/tablet runtime and expects a refreshed compact snapshot response.

Watch sends a forward navigation intent to the canonical phone/tablet runtime and expects a refreshed compact snapshot response. Payloads should preserve PlaybackPosition-derived media time and transcript segment context when the phone snapshot includes them.

Watch sends a backward navigation intent to the canonical phone/tablet runtime and expects a refreshed compact snapshot response. Payloads should preserve PlaybackPosition-derived media time and transcript segment context when the phone snapshot includes them.

Watch sends the selected resolved chapter id to the canonical phone/tablet runtime and expects a refreshed compact snapshot response. Payloads should preserve PlaybackPosition-derived media time and transcript segment context when the phone snapshot includes them.

Watch-started interjection remains hidden and rejected for Gate 3. If re-enabled later, the delegated command payload must preserve mediaTimeMs, durationMs, chapterId, and transcriptSegmentId from the phone snapshot rather than starting Watch-local recording.
Watch does not own recording state in Gate 3; finish is unavailable unless a future Watch-owned recording flow exists.
Watch exposes the iPhone summary sparkles action as a delegated AI intent; phone/tablet owns summary eligibility, provider calls, persistence, and pending job state.
Watch exposes the iPhone Discuss action as a delegated follow-up intent; phone/tablet owns prompt context, provider calls, persistence, and pending job state.

backendRequests.title: Publish state-aware available commands for compact Watch UI
backendRequests.details: CompactControlSnapshot now publishes availableCommands from state-aware compact exposed commands after command dispatch and snapshot reads.

backendRequests.title: Replay watch-tethered traces through compact dispatcher
backendRequests.details: Trace replay runs watch-tethered with a canonical phone-tablet-online runtime plus CompactControlDispatcher, similar to lock-screen-widget.

backendRequests.title: Clarify delegated interjection recording lifecycle
backendRequests.details: Real-device testing showed delegated Watch beginInterjection can complete the current item when the phone is locked. Gate 3 now hides and rejects Watch-started interjection.

backendRequests.title: Provide Watch-owned or background-safe interjection capture
backendRequests.details: Gate 4 should decide whether the Watch records/transcribes locally and syncs the interjection, or whether the phone can expose a proven background-safe recording command while locked.

backendRequests.title: Decide Watch chapter skip semantics
backendRequests.details: Compact dispatch now passes skip units through and SessionEngine supports chapter-unit skip behavior for text items with Listening Maps.

backendRequests.title: Publish compact timeline rows for Watch
backendRequests.details: CompactControlSnapshot now includes source chapters and generated AI/summary rows so the Watch can show timeline context below the primary controls.

backendRequests.title: Include PlaybackPosition anchors in tethered Watch compact snapshots and command payloads
backendRequests.details: Phone-to-Watch snapshots and delegated Watch commands should carry mediaTimeMs, durationMs, chapterId, progress, and transcriptSegmentId where available so chapter/progress display and future interjection delegation are anchored to real media time.

notes: Gate 3 does not own playback, recording, AI provider calls, persistence, transcription, or sync locally.
Gate 3 must not require Xcode project edits until the steward creates a Watch target scaffold.

The Watch playback interface should mirror the safe iPhone playback controls where possible: brief chapter or generated-turn label, skip back, play/pause, skip forward, AI summary when eligible, and Discuss.

The Watch compact snapshot should contain current item, target, chapter, playback status, progress, recording state, pending AI job state, last user turn type, and availableCommands; it must not require the current source excerpt.
traces/watch-chapter-navigation.json covers play/pause, chapter jump, chapter skip, boundary idempotence, and Discuss. Watch-started interjection is intentionally deferred to Gate 4.
Tethered Watch chapter/progress display should prefer PlaybackPosition-derived mediaTimeMs and durationMs, and preserve transcriptSegmentId/chapterId in delegated command payloads when available.
